location: Acceptance Criteria AC 2; Design Notes > Docs (Headless clean rule 'none of its e2e_next_cells has an e2e rerun_matrix entry'; 4th interim rule 'the next plan's e2e rerun_matrix reason'); contract Plan > Phase 2 'run e2e_next_cells, re-plan'
issue: `rerun_matrix` exists only in `--per-version` output. `ps-plan-layers.py` `main` builds it through `per_version_rollup` in per-version mode only. The canonical result is `{module, versions, newest_source, source_fingerprint, layers, rerun}` and has no `rerun_matrix`. The spec relies on `rerun_matrix` in three places but never says which plan mode those calls use: AC 2 ('both e2e `rerun_matrix`s'), the headless step-clean check ('one plan call with the same flags'), and the infra-cause carry rule. The contract does not say either. It requires `--per-version` only for calls that read `phase1_reuse`, and the hosting loop's separate run-scope E2E call and the Phase 2 re-plan have no stated mode.
implementation_impact: If the docs write the E2E step call or the Phase 2 re-plan without `--per-version`, the orchestrator finds no `rerun_matrix`. It then cannot apply the headless clean rule or the infra-carry rule, so a headless run cannot decide where to stop. The AC 2 test author also has to guess the mode. Run canonically, the test fails with a KeyError rather than testing scope.
suggestion: State in Design Notes > Plan or > Docs that every plan call whose E2E fields or `rerun_matrix` are read uses `--per-version`. That covers the hosting loop's run-scope call, the Phase 2 entry and loop calls, and the headless post-run call. The canonical call is used only for `layers.adversarial.reuse`. Write AC 2 as 'with `--per-version`, with and without `--versions 9.1 --browsers chromium`'. The alternative is to have canonical mode emit `rerun_matrix` as well, and say so.

location: Design Notes > Aggregate ('`reached` is emitted for every configured version only when `--session` is given') and Tasks > tests ('`reached` true from only a session ... record, false without one')
issue: The contract defines only `reached: false`: no session record and some cell lacking passing gate-grade evidence. The spec says a value is emitted for every configured version, but it never gives the rule for `true`. The open case is a version whose cells all have passing gate-grade evidence from an earlier session and no record in this session. Under 'any record of that session counts' that version would read false. Under the contract's second condition it is not false. The test bullet 'false without one' does not say whether the fixture version lacks passing evidence.
implementation_impact: An implementer has two plausible formulas: `has_session_record` alone, or `has_session_record or all_cells_passing`. They disagree exactly for evidence reused from an earlier session, which is the normal case after a headless re-call with no patch. Under the first formula, a fully proven version reports 'not reached: stopped at <step>' in the headless return, and psm-develop or psm-optimize treat it as unproven.
suggestion: Write the formula: `reached = (some configured cell of V has a record with this session) or (every configured cell of V has passing gate-grade evidence)`. Add a test row for 'all cells passing from an earlier session, no session record → `reached: true`'. Make the 'false without one' fixture explicitly lack passing evidence.

location: Design Notes > Docs > Headless ('`e2e_tier_reached` and `stopped at <step>` come from the plan call that chose the last step run or derived the `blocked-*` step (the last plan call when none ran)') vs cell-contract.md > Headless bullet 3 ('`e2e_tier_reached` = `{tier, step}` from the last plan call')
issue: The spec changes the contract's source for `e2e_tier_reached`. In headless, the last plan call is the post-run cleanliness check, and it already derives the next step: for example `focus`, tier 0, after a failed gate run. The contract's literal rule therefore reports the step after the stop. The spec reports the step that ran, which matches tier-matrix.md ('stops at the first step that is not clean, reporting `e2e_tier_reached`'). The two sources disagree, and the spec settles it silently even though 'Ask First' covers changing a contract rule.
implementation_impact: A docs author who checks the contract finds a different rule from the spec and has to pick one. Headless callers' `not reached: stopped at <step>` texts and `e2e_tier_reached` values differ between the two readings, for example `gate`/1 vs `focus`/0 after a tier-1 failure.
suggestion: Mark this as a deliberate reading in Design Notes: 'contract Headless "last plan call" read as the call that chose the step run, per tier-matrix Rules', and add a deferred-work note to amend the contract wording. Otherwise follow the contract literally.

location: Design Notes > Docs > Headless ('The four headless callers' SKILL.md: `not reached` is unproven.') vs cell-contract.md > Docs to update (headless callers)
issue: The spec restates the callers' change as one sentence and drops two contract items. First, 'never written back into a plan as one': a `not reached` version is neither a pass nor a per-version finding. Second, the psm-optimize specifics: Profil records each version's `e2e_state` and `reason` in the baseline, and in Verifikasi a version that is `not reached` in the baseline or the after run is reported as not comparable, never as 'no new failure'. psm-optimize/SKILL.md today records only 'status psm-validate awal per versi (lolos/gagal)' and judges delta as 'tak ada kegagalan baru'.
implementation_impact: An implementer who follows the spec bullet edits four SKILL.md files with one line each. psm-optimize then still counts a `not reached` version in the after run as 'no new failure' against its baseline, which is the false green the contract item exists to prevent.
suggestion: Replace the bullet with the contract's full text for the callers. At minimum add 'never written back into a plan as a pass or finding' and the psm-optimize baseline and Verifikasi rules. Also add the psm-optimize line to the Verification manual checklist.

location: I/O & Edge-Case Matrix, row 'Clean module' ('aggregate `ready` true')
issue: Aggregate `ready` defaults to requiring every layer: static, flashlight, adversarial, e2e, plus scenario when the module ships scenarios. The row gives only E2E histories. It does not say whether the test passes `--require e2e` or builds passing Layer 1, 2 and 3 files.
implementation_impact: With E2E histories alone, the aggregate reports `ready: false` because static is required, so the test author has to guess the fixture. A test with `--require e2e` proves the E2E part. A test with full layer fixtures is much larger and couples this slice to Layer 1, 2 and 3 shapes.
suggestion: Write the row as 'aggregate with `--require e2e` (static from a minimal `<module>-static.json`) → `ready` true', or name the fixture files explicitly.

location: Design Notes > Docs > Headless ('config copy resets the canary only when it is well-formed ... and outside the caller's set')
issue: 'Well-formed' is defined, but the comparison behind 'outside the caller's set' is not. Plan, runner and aggregate apply the canary normalizer: trimmed parts, version equal to a configured string, browser lower-cased. The headless copy is written by the model, not a script, and the spec does not say whether its comparison lower-cases the browser or trims the parts. Example: canary `9.1:Firefox` with caller set 9.1 × chromium,firefox. The normalizer reads it as inside the set. A case-sensitive comparison reads it as outside, resets it, and silently changes the canary to 9.1:chromium.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator applies this by judgment. Depending on how it compares, a valid configured canary is either kept or replaced by the default, which changes which cell is tier 0 for the headless run. The only trace is an assumption line.
suggestion: Add: 'compare as the normalizer does: trimmed version as an exact string against the caller's versions, trimmed browser lower-cased against the caller's browsers'.

location: Design Notes > Plan ('`--browsers` ... default from `--config`, else `chromium,firefox`') and Code Map ('`CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST` (unchanged; `psm_e2e_browsers` → `browsers` already maps)')
issue: The plan's `main` calls `fl.apply_config_file`, which treats a flag as explicit only when its value differs from the argparse default. The spec does not fix the argparse default of the new `--browsers`. If it is the literal `"chromium,firefox"`, an explicit `--browsers chromium,firefox` is silently replaced by the config's `psm_e2e_browsers`. The 'explicit flag wins' rule then fails for that value, and an out-of-config browser is no longer rejected with exit 2.
implementation_impact: The behaviour depends on a hidden choice. A test of `--browsers` outside the configured set can pass or fail depending on the default the implementer picked.
suggestion: Say that `--browsers` has argparse default `None`, that `apply_config_file` fills it from `psm_e2e_browsers`, and that it falls back to `chromium,firefox` only when both are absent. Then a given `""` stays explicit and exits 2.

location: Acceptance Criteria AC 1 (generated histories over config 3×2)
issue: The combination space is 4^6 base histories × 4 F variants, about 16,384 derivations. The AC says 'when the plan derives each' but not whether the test calls the new pure derivation function or the CLI. It also leaves the `pass` record's content open: passing gate-grade (`authored_assertions` ≥ 1, empty notes) or any `pass`. That choice decides whether the not-gradeable branches are exercised.
implementation_impact: A CLI-per-case test runs one subprocess per derivation, about 16k process starts plus history file I/O. That takes far longer than the other test files and may time out the Verification loop. If the `pass` content is left implicit, two implementers produce tests with different coverage of steps 2 and 4.
suggestion: State that AC 1 calls the pure step-derivation function in-process with in-memory records. Specify that `pass` records are passing gate-grade, and optionally add an `authored_assertions` 0 variant.

location: I/O & Edge-Case Matrix (loop-back rows) vs tier-matrix.md > Rules > Loop-back ('When V is the canary version, step 2 already covers the canary cell and step 3 is skipped')
issue: This load-bearing tier-matrix claim has no I/O row or test. It holds only because a `cold-version` pass on the canary version leaves the canary passing gate-grade, so step 4 `gate` matches before step 6. In the interim, `cold-version` is reachable only with hand-written warm records, and nothing pins that the plan goes straight from `cold-version` [9.1 ×2] to `gate`.
implementation_impact: A derivation that, for example, recomputes `cold-canary` from a stale-pass rule before checking `gate` would wrongly add an extra canary boot after a canary-version loop-back, and no listed test would catch it.
suggestion: Add an I/O row: 'tier-1 fail 9.1:firefox; patch; warm pass 9.1:firefox → `cold-version` [9.1 ×2]; both cold pass → `gate` [1.7.8 ×2, 8.1 ×2]' (no `cold-canary`).

location: Design Notes > Docs ('Orchestration per contract Plan and tier-matrix: hosting version ...')
issue: The hosting version is defined from `e2e_focus_cell` at the moment the orchestrator enters Phase 1 (session start or loop-back). The current docs start Fase 1 directly with per-version plan calls, whose E2E fields are not read, so no plan call yet exists that yields `e2e_focus_cell` before the loops start. Neither the spec nor the contract names the session-start call: its flags, `--versions`/`--browsers` = run scope, mode. Nor do they say whether the hosting loop finishes before the other versions' loops start, or whether they interleave.
implementation_impact: The docs author has to invent the entry sequence. Different choices change which version hosts tier 0 when a cell is already failing at session start, for example a failing record left by an earlier session. They also change whether Layer 2 and 5 boots of other versions compete with the canary boot for slots.
suggestion: Add one sentence: 'At session start and on each loop-back, the orchestrator takes `e2e_focus_cell` from a run-scope `--per-version` plan call (session start: a fresh one; loop-back: the Phase 2 call that derived the tier-0 step). The hosting loop runs to its end before the other in-scope versions' loops.'
